stem: Chlorate(V) ions are powerful oxidising agents.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The reduction of chlorate(V) ions, $\text{ClO}_3^-$, with $\text{SO}_2$ forms chlorine dioxide, $\text{ClO}_2$, and sulfate ions, $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$, as the only products.

Construct an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Chlorine dioxide, $\text{ClO}_2$, disproportionates with hydroxide ions, $\text{OH}^-\text{(aq)}$, to form a mixture of $\text{ClO}_2^-$ and $\text{ClO}_3^-$ ions.

$$2\text{ClO}_2 + 2\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{ClO}_2^- + \text{ClO}_3^- + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Explain, using this reaction as an example, what is meant by disproportionation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the ionic half-equations for the reaction in (b)(i).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: A lithium-iodine electrochemical cell can be used to generate electricity for a heart pacemaker. The cell consists of a lithium electrode and an inert electrode immersed in body fluids. When current flows lithium is oxidised and iodine is reduced.
parts.text: Use the Data Booklet to write half-equations for the reactions taking place at the two electrodes. Hence write the overall equation for when a current flows.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Use the Data Booklet to calculate the $E^\ominus_{\text{cell}}$ for this cell.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
A current of $2.5 \times 10^{-5}\text{ A}$ is drawn from this cell.

Calculate the time taken for $0.10\text{ g}$ of lithium electrode to be used up. Assume the current remains constant throughout this period.
